title: Laundry detergent powder
subtitle: A washing soda and soap-flakes blend for cold and warm washes
excerpt: Laundry detergent powder is a dry blend of washing soda, bicarbonate of soda, and grated soap flakes that dissolves in the machine drum and washes a full load in cold or warm water. No optical brighteners or fragrance, which makes it suitable for sensitive skin. Makes 1 kg, enough for about twenty-five standard washes.
sourceNotes: Washing soda and soap-flakes laundry formula: Natural Cleaning Solutions by Rachel Ogden (2012). Sodium carbonate (washing soda) as a water softener and alkaline builder: standard laundry chemistry, documented in OECD Chemical Safety Assessment (2016). Bicarbonate of soda as a mild deodoriser: widely documented. Grated bar soap as a surfactant base: traditional washing formula. Note: soap-based laundry powder can leave grey residue on dark fabrics washed repeatedly at very low temperatures (30°C and below), rinse once extra if grey cast develops.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~1 kg laundry powder (~25 washes at 40 g per wash)
recipe.batchNotes: Make large batches and store in an airtight container.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ready to use immediately. Grate the soap a day ahead if it is very soft, letting it dry slightly helps it grate to a finer consistency.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: One year in an airtight container kept dry. The washing soda and bicarbonate absorb humidity from the air and clump if left exposed. Stir or break up any clumps before measuring.

glossaryTerms.definition: Sodium carbonate, an alkaline cleaning agent and water softener used in laundry to remove grease and boost the action of soap. Significantly stronger than bicarbonate of soda, handle with dry hands as it can irritate damp skin.

items.prepNote: sodium carbonate; the main cleaning builder and water softener; not the same as bicarbonate of soda
deodoriser and mild softener; also reduces the harshness of the washing soda on delicates
plain unscented soap flakes (or finely grated unscented bar soap); the surfactant that lifts and suspends soil

content.text: Combine the washing soda, bicarbonate of soda, and soap flakes in a large bowl. Mix thoroughly until evenly distributed. Pour into a sealed container. Wearing dry gloves when handling washing soda is good practice, it irritates damp hands.

Add 30 to 40 g per load directly to the drum (not the detergent drawer, soap flakes can clog drawers over time). Works well at 40°C and above. At 30°C some soap residue may remain in the drum; if you wash consistently at low temperatures, run an empty hot wash monthly to clear any build-up.
One year in a sealed, dry container. Stir or break up any clumps before measuring. Use a dry scoop, water in the container causes the powder to set solid.
